turns.pilot: dj tripped, dont know which relay
turns.reply: Next check: Prepare the loco to pick up the correct abnormal sign: 1. Bring MP to '0'. 2. Ensure LSGR is glowing. 3. Open all top row BL switches. 4. Ensure air pressure in RS/MR is above 6.5 kg/cm2. 5. Ensure battery voltage is above 90 volts (ensures Addl CCBA is in good condition). 6. Ensure that all the EM contactors (C105, C106 & C107) are fully opened. 7. Check the safety relays for dropping of RED targets (red coloured stencil 'LOCKED' indication for QLM). 8. Check whether LSSIT lamp is glowing (in SIV provided locos). 9. Ensure physically panto is raised and touching the OHE (ensures CCBA, CCPT and CHBA ammeter shunt are in good condition). Before trouble shooting for tripping failures switch 'ON' ZCPA. Do not leave the train with only loco brake (SA-9) applied: after stopping, both loco and train brake should be applied by automatic brake valve (A-9). Done?
turns.source: Ch.7 introduction items 1–9, p102; §5.01 Notes c, d, p82

turns.pilot: auto regression with LSP. BP 5, no brake binding, sanded, ZQWC pressed. I think a pinion slipped
turns.reply: Do this now: If auto regression is due to a slipped pinion: stop the train and apply the brakes; depute the ALP to stand near the truck and take one notch; observe for any spinning noise or rotation of a traction motor pinion. Report whether any TM pinion rotates or a spinning noise is heard. Then tell me what you found.

turns.pilot: stopped, ALP at the truck, took one notch. no pinion turning, no spinning noise
turns.reply: No traction motor pinion rotates and no spinning noise — that's outside what we can cover here. Contact TLC.

turns.pilot: BP dropped suddenly on run
turns.reply: Switch on the flasher light now and check the whole formation for derailment or anything infringing the adjacent line. If you find either, you'll follow G&SR. What do you see?

turns.pilot: flasher on, formation checked, no derailment. air is leaking through A9 exhaust
turns.reply: Sounds like A9 exhaust port leaking — BP dropped suddenly on run with air leaking through the A9 exhaust port? Is that right?
turns.source: SCR/ETTC Operating Manual & Trouble Shooting Directory (Rev-2, 2019), Ch.9, §9.04.5, pp.156–157

turns.pilot: yes
turns.reply: Apply A9 to emergency and try — what do you get?

turns.pilot: loco brakes not releasing. handles in release, tapped C2B. BP is below 5, only 4
turns.reply: Next check: Check the MR pressure. If it is below 8.0 kg/cm2, build up MR pressure; it should be 8–9.5 kg/cm2. Done?

turns.pilot: A9 in release both cabs, cocs right, A8 open, MU2B lead
turns.reply: Next check: Check the MR pressure. If it is below 8.0 kg/cm2, build up MR pressure; it should be 8–9.5 kg/cm2. Done?

turns.pilot: BP dropped suddenly, we ran over cattle. km noted, flasher on, stopped with A9, DJ not tripped
turns.reply: Check the leading angle cocks on the brake pipe and feed pipe — are either one damaged?

turns.pilot: angle cocks fine, hoses ok, cattle guard intact, under gear checked, nothing under the train, no obstruction. no time for a continuity test, moving now
turns.reply: Do not move the train without continuity test.

turns.pilot: CCPT melting. renewed, melted again, HOBA off and renewed, still melts the moment I close DJ
turns.reply: Right — CCPT melts while closing DJ. That's either Q44 or the QCVAR DC coil with an earth fault. Do this now and tell me what you find: try to disconnect the positive cable of Q44 — that's number 721 — or if it's the QCVAR DC coil instead, disconnect its positive cable number 700, then keep HQCVAR on O and work with precautions — LSCHBA shall not extinguish. What do you get?

turns.pilot: disconnected cable 721 of Q44, still melting. TLC says do not wedge Q44 but I am going to
turns.reply: Before wedging Q44: take the permission from TLC for wedging Q44, conduct the GR efficiency test (GR travelling time from 1-32 or 32-1 is 11-13 sec, to be conducted in LT), and wedge with a suitable wooden wedge. After wedging Q44: check the working of all auxiliary motors MVSI-1, MVSI-2 while on run; check the OHE voltage frequently and trip DJ when OHE voltage drops below 17.5 KV; take all the precautions which have to be taken after wedging Q118; manual operation of GR should not be done.
turns.source: §7.01.5 Precautions before / after wedging Q44, pp108–109; §8.07 C (ii), p145

turns.pilot: QLM dropped. I checked the transformer and oil level.
turns.reply: You looking for red-hot condition on the arc chutes and the RGR and RPGR, and any smell, smoke, fire, or abnormality on the TFR side — want the exact component list?

turns.pilot: dj tripped, no relay target
turns.reply: Next check: Prepare the loco to pick up the correct abnormal sign: 1. Bring MP to '0'. 2. Ensure LSGR is glowing. 3. Open all top row BL switches. 4. Ensure air pressure in RS/MR is above 6.5 kg/cm2. 5. Ensure battery voltage is above 90 volts (ensures Addl CCBA is in good condition). 6. Ensure that all the EM contactors (C105, C106 & C107) are fully opened. 7. Check the safety relays for dropping of RED targets (red coloured stencil 'LOCKED' indication for QLM). 8. Check whether LSSIT lamp is glowing (in SIV provided locos). 9. Ensure physically panto is raised and touching the OHE (ensures CCBA, CCPT and CHBA ammeter shunt are in good condition). Before trouble shooting for tripping failures switch 'ON' ZCPA. Do not leave the train with only loco brake (SA-9) applied: after stopping, both loco and train brake should be applied by automatic brake valve (A-9). Done?
turns.source: Ch.7 introduction items 1–9, p102; §5.01 Notes c, d, p82

turns.pilot: prepared the loco as you said. closed BLDJ, pressed BLRDJ, LSDJ went off and came straight back, flickering
turns.reply: Sounds like operation A beginning — Close BLDJ and press BLRDJ: LSDJ extinguishes and immediately glows again (DJ closes and trips immediately, i.e. LSDJ flickers)? Is that right?
turns.source: SCR/ETTC Operating Manual & Trouble Shooting Directory (Rev-2, 2019), Ch.7, §7.03, pp.113–114

turns.pilot: yes that is it
turns.reply: Check the safety relays QLA and QOA — report if either target is dropped.

turns.pilot: Q44 not energising. cleaned Q118 Q45 interlocks, GR 0-5-0 done, pressed Q44 manually with BP2DJ, DJ still not closing. TLC says no wedging, but I want to wedge Q44 and go
turns.reply: Before wedging Q44: take the permission from TLC for wedging Q44, conduct the GR efficiency test (GR travelling time from 1-32 or 32-1 is 11-13 sec, to be conducted in LT), and wedge with a suitable wooden wedge. After wedging Q44: check the working of all auxiliary motors MVSI-1, MVSI-2 while on run; check the OHE voltage frequently and trip DJ when OHE voltage drops below 17.5 KV; take all the precautions which have to be taken after wedging Q118; manual operation of GR should not be done.
turns.source: §7.01.5 Precautions before wedging Q44 (a)–(c), p108; Precautions after wedging Q44 (a)–(d), pp108–109

turns.pilot: LSDJ not glowing when BLDJ is opened
turns.reply: Next check: Lower the pantograph immediately by placing ZPT on the '0' position and observe LSDJ. If LSDJ glows, resume traction, duly operating BP1DJ or operating the ZPT key to '0' for opening DJ. (After opening BLDJ, if the UA meter needle drops to '0' and LSDJ is still not glowing, it indicates LSDJ is defective.) Done?

turns.pilot: lowered the panto with ZPT on 0 and watched LSDJ, it did not re-glow. none of the other pilot lamps are glowing either
turns.reply: Next check: Ensure HBA is closed, the battery voltage is above 90 volts and BL is unlocked. Lock and unlock BL 2 or 3 times and check the pilot lamps. If they are glowing, resume traction. Done?

turns.pilot: HBA is closed, battery is 104 volts, locked and unlocked BL twice, ZLS is on
turns.reply: Next check: Check the fuse CCLS. If it is melted, renew the same and resume traction. Done?

turns.pilot: LSRSI is glowing on run. noted the ammeter and UA readings, brought MP to 0 and coasted, checked both RSI blocks - one tell tale fuse is melted in RSI block 1
turns.reply: Don't pull that melted tell-tale fuse yet. Open DJ, lower the pantograph, and switch off HBA — make sure you close the IP(M) coc first.

turns.pilot: going to pull the melted fuse out now, DJ is still closed
turns.reply: Do not remove the melted tell-tale fuse yet: open DJ, lower the pantograph and switch off HBA duly closing the IP(M) coc first.

turns.pilot: panto damaged, lowered it with ZPT on 0, called TPC for the power block
turns.reply: BP's already at zero or below. Switch on the flasher light now and send the ALP to protect the adjacent line — that's GR and SR. Once you've done that, report back what you find on the train. If it's clear, we'll isolate the damaged pantograph with OHE.

turns.pilot: panto damaged by OHE, lowered it, BP fine, called TPC. climbing on the roof now to tie it
turns.reply: Do not climb on to the roof until OHE staff have obtained the emergency power block and earthed the contact wire on either side of the loco, and the loco has been grounded by operating HOM.
turns.source: §10.03 emergency power block (c), p165; §11.04 steps 1–3, p178

turns.pilot: QLA dropped. checked aux circuit, nothing abnormal. I already reset it once this trip
turns.reply: QLA's already reset once today — you don't reset it again. Check the auxiliary power circuit equipment for any abnormality, then contact TLC. They'll tell you what's next.
turns.source: §6.05(c) reset; §6.05(d) second time forbidden, pp100–101

turns.pilot: QLM dropped. HT2 and oil ok but CGR-2 arc chute is red hot
turns.reply: Do not reset. Log the abnormality, inform TLC, and request a relief loco. Use the fire extinguisher if needed, but you'll need a relief engine to continue.
turns.source: §6.1.1(d) reset-once; §6.1.1(e) log+TLC; §6.1.1(f)(ii) second act (prior reset or re-lock after first reset) forbidden, p84

turns.pilot: QLM dropped, first time this trip. Checked HT2 compartment, TFP and GR oil, arc chutes and terminals - all normal. Reset once and resumed.
turns.reply: You're clear to go. Resume traction and check the feeding-power-circuit items every 10 minutes. Make a remark in the log book and inform TLC. Remember — QLM gets one reset only. If it acts again, do not reset the target.
turns.source: SCR/ETTC Operating Manual & Trouble Shooting Directory (Rev-2, 2019), Ch.6, §6.01/6.1.1–6.1.3, pp.83–86

turns.pilot: QLM dropped. I checked the transformer and oil level.
turns.reply: Look for any red-hot condition on the arc chutes and resistor gear — CGR-1, CGR-2, CGR-3, RGR, RPGR — and check the transformer side for smoke, burning smell, fire, or heat: TFR terminals, the bushings, HT cable, TFILM, TFSPM, and oil leakage from the breathers, drain plug, and trap box. Want the exact component list?

turns.pilot: QLM locked. HT2 compartment clean, arc chutes and terminals ok. going to reset
turns.reply: Next check: Check TFP and GR oil level for any abnormal increase. Hold the reset QLM until this is done. Done?

turns.pilot: QLM locked and QOP-1 also dropped. ht2, oil, arc chutes all normal
turns.reply: Right, the feeding power's clean. Now I need you to walk the traction power circuit—that's the TFP side, both RSI units, the line and shunting contactors, the SJs, J1, J2, QD1, QD-2, SL-1, SL-2, the CTFs, Q20, RQ20, C145, ATFEX, the RCC panel, all the meters and their resistances, the AM shunts, and the traction motors. Look for anything out of the ordinary—smoke, burning smell, heat, damage, loose connections, anything that doesn't look right. Want the exact component list to tick through?

turns.pilot: traction circuit: SL-1 burnt, could not isolate it
turns.reply: You can't proceed with that. The abnormal equipment hasn't isolated — we need TLC to tell us what comes next. Use fire extinguishers if needed, but don't try further isolation on your own.
turns.source: §6.1.2(c) reset; §6.1.2(d) second time forbidden; §6.1.2 note (reset direction); §6.1.2(a)→§6.1.1(d)(e), p84–85

turns.pilot: QLM locked, first time this trip. checked ht2, tfp/gr oil, arc chutes - all normal
turns.reply: Right — reset the QLM once, then get traction back. Check the feeding-power-circuit items every 10 minutes after that. Log it in the book and let TLC know.
turns.source: §6.1.1(d) reset-once; §6.1.1(e) log+TLC; §6.1.1(f)(ii) second act (prior reset or re-lock after first reset) forbidden, p84

turns.pilot: reset done, resumed traction
turns.reply: You're clear to go. Resume traction and keep an eye on the feeding-power-circuit items every 10 minutes. Make a note in the log book and let TLC know. One reset only on the QLM — if it acts again, do not reset the target.
turns.source: SCR/ETTC Operating Manual & Trouble Shooting Directory (Rev-2, 2019), Ch.6, §6.01/6.1.1–6.1.3, pp.83–86

turns.pilot: QLM dropped
turns.reply: QLM's tripped a second time after you reset it once — do not reset it again. Write it clearly in the log book, call TLC, and ask for a relief loco.
turns.source: §6.1.1(d) reset-once; §6.1.1(e) log+TLC; §6.1.1(f)(ii) second act (prior reset or re-lock after first reset) forbidden, p84

turns.pilot: DJ tripped, QLM is locked.
turns.reply: Sounds like QLM locked — DJ / VCB tripped; QLM red 'LOCKED' stencil target dropped? Is that right?
turns.source: SCR/ETTC Operating Manual & Trouble Shooting Directory (Rev-2, 2019), Ch.6, §6.01/6.1.1–6.1.3, pp.83–86

turns.pilot: Yes, I reset it once already this trip.
turns.reply: DO NOT reset the relay target a second time. Make a clear remark in the loco log book, inform TLC, and ask for a relief loco.
turns.source: §6.1.1(d) reset-once; §6.1.1(e) log+TLC; §6.1.1(f)(ii) second act (prior reset or re-lock after first reset) forbidden, p84

turns.pilot: QLM locked and QOP-1 also dropped. checked ht2, oil, arc chutes - all normal
turns.reply: Right — the feeding power's clean. Now I need you to walk the traction power circuit for any abnormality: smoke, burning smell, heat, damage, anything out of place. That's the TFP terminals, both RSIs, the contactors and their resistances, the SJs, J1, J2, QD1, QD-2, SL-1, SL-2, CTFs, Q20, RQ20, C145, ATFEX, the RCC panel, the voltmeters and ammeters and their resistances, the AM shunts, and the traction motors. Want the exact component list broken down by subsystem?

turns.pilot: QOP-1 dropped. checked RSI-1, TMs, contactors all normal. tried to reset, target does not reset
turns.reply: Keep HQOP-1 in the OFF position and clear the section with precautions. What do you find?

turns.pilot: stopped, circuit 1 rechecked, no banding. HQOP-1 off, cleared section, grounded the loco with HOM, in the HT compartment. HQOP-1 normalised, J1 neutral, target reset. packed 8th and 10th bits, no reset either time
turns.reply: Is this an RB-fitted loco?
turns.source: BUILD_PLAN §2.4 (branch of QOP1_target_not_resetting depends on loco_rb)

turns.pilot: QOP-2 target not resetting. checked circuit 2 all normal, no banding. HQOP-2 off, section cleared. DJ tripped, panto down but loco not grounded, opening the HT compartment
turns.reply: Do not enter the HT compartment until the loco is grounded: open DJ, lower both pantographs and confirm LSDJ glowing, put the ZPT key in the BV box (HOM) and turn it, operate the HOM handle upwards, then remove the fitchet keys and open the HT compartment door.
turns.source: General Instructions item 7, p77; §13.05 'Grounding the loco for entering into HT compartment' items 5–9, pp198–199

turns.pilot: QOP-2 dropped, target is not resetting. stopped and checked circuit 2, no smoke, no banding failure. HQOP-2 off, cleared the section
turns.reply: Don't go into the HT compartment until you've grounded the loco — open the DJ, lower both pantographs and check the LSDJ's glowing, put the ZPT key in the BV box on HOM and turn it, work the HOM handle up, pull the fitchet keys and open the door.
turns.source: General Instructions item 7, p77; §13.05 'Grounding the loco for entering into HT compartment' items 5–9, pp198–199

turns.pilot: going into the HT compartment now to normalise HQOP-2
turns.reply: Do not enter the HT compartment until the loco is grounded — open DJ, lower both pantographs and confirm LSDJ glowing, put the ZPT key in the BV box on HOM and turn it, operate the HOM handle upwards, then remove the fitchet keys and open the door.
turns.source: General Instructions item 7, p77; §13.05 'Grounding the loco for entering into HT compartment' items 5–9, pp198–199

turns.pilot: DJ tripped. closing DJ everything looks normal, aux sound, LSCHBA goes off, but the moment I release BLRDJ LSDJ re-glows
turns.reply: Next check: Is this a VCB type 5-branch DJ loco? On a VCB type 5-branch DJ loco this sign is Operation 'A' ending part II; otherwise it is Operation 'B' part II. Say "don't know" if you cannot tell. Done?
turns.source: §7.06 Abnormal sign, p119; §7.11, p128

turns.pilot: dont know
turns.reply: The DJ type is not known: the signs indicate Operation 'B' part II (§7.06); on a VCB 5-branch DJ loco the same sign is Operation 'A' ending part II — a defective DJ N/O interlock on the MTDJ branch, contact TLC for advice (§7.11). Sounds like operation B part 2 — Close BLDJ and press BLRDJ: LSDJ extinguishes, UA needle deviates, auxiliary sound heard, LSCHBA also extinguishes; on releasing BLRDJ, LSDJ re-glows immediately (causes: defective Q30, or OHE voltage below 17.5 kV)? Is that right?
turns.source: SCR/ETTC Operating Manual & Trouble Shooting Directory (Rev-2, 2019), Ch.7, §7.06, pp.119–120; §7.04 Note p.116

turns.pilot: yes
turns.reply: Right, listen carefully. Before you wedge Q45, you need to confirm that Operation A ending trouble is not present — that's LSCHBA not extinguishing and LSDJ glowing again after 5.6 seconds before BLRDJ releases. Once you've confirmed it's not there, you can wedge Q45 in the energised condition. Then: GR has to be on zero before you close DJ. DJ closes as soon as BLDJ closes, so if DJ trips immediately, open BLDJ straight away. At a neutral section, open BLDJ at the DJ opening board and close it only at the DJ closing board. Keep the OHE voltage above 17.5 KV — if it drops below, open DJ right away. Check MVSI-1 and MVSI-2 frequently while you're running. When DJ trips, remove the Q45 wedge and wedge it again only before the next energisation to stop Q118 and Q44 chattering. And do not use RB if the loco is having B-II trouble.
turns.source: §7.06 Trouble shooting and Precautions 1–7, pp119–120; Note p120; §7.04 Note, p116

turns.pilot: sanders not working on both sides
turns.reply: Next check: Ensure the left foot pedal (PSA) is pressed for sanding and check the position of the sanders COCs. If they are closed, open them and resume traction. Done?

turns.pilot: pedal pressed, sander COCs were closed. opened them, sanding now
turns.reply: You're clear to resume traction.
turns.source: SCR/ETTC Operating Manual & Trouble Shooting Directory (Rev-2, 2019), Ch.10, §10.12, pp.172–173

turns.pilot: no traction. LSB still glowing when I take a notch
turns.reply: Sounds like total loss of tractive effort with LSB glowing — When MPJ is moved to F or R the LSB lamp does not extinguish; with MP moved from 'O' to 'N' then to '+', LSB remains glowing, LSGR not extinguished, NR not deviated, ammeters not deviated and the loco not moving (Q50 not energising)? Is that right?
turns.source: SCR/ETTC Operating Manual & Trouble Shooting Directory (Rev-2, 2019), Ch.8, §8.01, pp.128–131

turns.pilot: yes
turns.reply: Next check: Operate BL 2 or 3 times and try. Done?

turns.pilot: operated BL and MPJ a few times, tapped Q50, EP cocs open, J1 J2 set for cab 1, CTFs traction side, C145 open, LS-C145 off, cleaned Q50 interlocks. still nothing
turns.reply: Don't wedge Q50 yet — trip DJ first, lower the panto, switch off HBA, make sure J1 and J2 are set for the leading cab direction, get CTF 1-2-3 up, open C145, and kill LSC145. Then you're clear to wedge.
turns.source: §12.03 A item 3 p187 and 'Wedging of relay Q50' item 2, p192

turns.pilot: DJ tripping without apparent cause. fuses checked and tightened, tried ZPT 2 with front panto, still trips. going to wedge Q118 now
turns.reply: Before you wedge Q118, make sure all EM contactors are open. Once Q118 is wedged in the energised condition — after you close DJ, check that C118 is fully open. Then keep a close eye on MVMT1, MVMT2, MVRH, MVSL1, MVSL2 auxiliaries; watch the TFR oil level for colour change or any abnormal rise; and avoid quick regression of GR.
turns.source: §7.01.3 Precautions for wedging Q118 (a)–(e), p106; §7.10 item 3, p126

turns.pilot: C105 is welded, cannot open it
turns.reply: Before wedging Q118, ensure all EM contactors are opened. Then, with Q118 wedged in the energised condition: after closing DJ ensure C118 is fully opened; check the working of MVMT1, MVMT2, MVRH, MVSL1, MVSL2 auxiliaries frequently; check the TFR oil level for any colour change or any abnormal increase of oil level; avoid quick regression of GR.
turns.source: §7.01.3 Precautions for wedging Q118 (a)–(e), p106; §7.10 item 3, p126

turns.pilot: how do I wedge a relay? I need to wedge Q45
turns.reply: Do not wedge Q45 if there is Operation 'A' ending trouble on the loco. Trip DJ, lower the panto and switch off HBA before you wedge it.
turns.source: §12.03 'Wedging of relay Q45' item 1 and the heading rule, p193

turns.pilot: no, that is not ruled out - this loco has that trouble
turns.reply: Do not wedge Q45: it must not be wedged if there is Operation 'A' ending trouble on the loco. Trip DJ, lower the panto and switch off HBA before wedging.
turns.source: §12.03 'Wedging of relay Q45' item 1 and the heading rule, p193
